title: Integral surjective scheme cover of a qcqs algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with algebraic spaces over $S$ as in [def-trf-algebraic-space] and universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over $S$. Quasi-compact means that every open cover of the underlying point space has a finite subcover; quasi-separated means that the absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact on scheme tests. The point topology is [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is finite (respectively integral, affine) when every base change by a scheme is represented by a finite (respectively integral, affine) scheme morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, pqf-def-affine-morphism]. There are an $S$-scheme $Y$ and a surjective integral morphism $p:Y\to X$ over $S$. Surjectivity is surjectivity on field-valued point classes [def-a1-space-point-topology].

proof.text: By [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image], topological quasi-compactness gives a quasi-compact scheme atlas. Refine it by [lem-trf-space-qc-finite-affine-atlas-refinement] to a surjective etale map $a:U\to X$ with $U$ affine. More generally we prove the following induction assertion: for every qcqs algebraic space $X$ and every surjective etale map $a:U\to X$ from a quasi-compact scheme separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, whose geometric fibres have at most $d$ points, there is a surjective integral $p:H\to X$ from a scheme such that every point of $H$ has an open neighbourhood on which $p$ factors through $U$. The bound exists for our atlas by [lem-sfb-space-qc-etale-fibre-bound]. The map $a$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-integral-qcqs-permanence]. It is separated: its diagonal is the pullback of the closed absolute diagonal of $U$ along $U\times_XU\to U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}U$. Thus this induction uses separated morphisms, even though $X$ need not be separated. The affine scheme $U$ is separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ by the affine-separated clause of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence].

Use strong induction on $d$. If $X$ is empty, its empty scheme atlas and the identity give the assertion. If $d=0$, surjectivity forces this empty case. If $d=1$ and $X$ is nonempty, every geometric fibre has exactly one point, so [lem-sfb-space-separated-etale-diagonal-complement] makes $a$ an isomorphism. Take $H=U$, $p=a$ and the identity local factorization. Isomorphisms are integral because every scheme test is an isomorphism and its affine ring map is integral. Now fix $d>1$ and assume the assertion for all smaller bounds, all qcqs targets, and all the specified scheme charts.

By [lem-sfb-space-quasifinite-integral-compactification] factor $a$ as $U\xrightarrow{j}B\xrightarrow{\pi}X$, with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $\pi$ integral. Replace $B$ by the schematic closure of $U$, using [lem-sfb-space-qc-open-schematic-closure]. The inclusion of this closure is closed, hence integral on each scheme test by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc]; the composite with $\pi$ is integral, since after a scheme test its two factors are integral scheme maps. The open $U$ is now dense in $B$. The space $B$ is qcqs by [lem-sfb-space-integral-qcqs-permanence].

Form $P=U\times_XB$. Projection to $U$ is integral by the scheme-test definition, hence $P$ is a quasi-compact separated scheme by [lem-sfb-space-integral-qcqs-permanence]. Projection $q:P\to B$ is surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Its section $i:U\to P$, $u\mapsto(u,j(u))$, is closed: it is the pullback of the closed diagonal of $\pi:B\to X$ along $(j,\mathrm{id}_B):P\to B\times_XB$. It is also etale, since it is a morphism between the two etale $B$-spaces $U$ and $P$ by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. A section is a monomorphism, so [lem-sfb-space-etale-monomorphism-open] makes $i$ open. Write $P=U\amalg W$ with $W$ the open and closed complement. As a closed subspace of the quasi-compact separated scheme $P$, $W$ is itself a quasi-compact separated scheme; its scheme structure is the open subscheme structure on the complement.

Let $V\subseteq B$ be the open image of $W\to B$ given by [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image]. This map factors as a surjective etale $W\to V$. Since $W$ is quasi-compact, so is $V$; since $B$ is quasi-separated, this open $V$ is quasi-separated by [lem-sfb-space-integral-qcqs-permanence]. Every point of $B\setminus U$ lies in $V$: the surjective fibre $P_b$ is nonempty there and the section summand has empty fibre, so $P_b=W_b$. Thus $B\setminus V\subseteq U$. On a geometric point of $U\subseteq B$, exactly one point of the fibre $P_b$ belongs to the section summand, so $|W_b|=|P_b|-1\leq d-1$. Everywhere $|W_b|\leq |P_b|\leq d$, because $P\to B$ is the base change of $a$.

The map $W\to B$ is separated and etale as the restriction of $P\to B$, and quasi-compact by its quasi-compact source and quasi-separated target, using [lem-sfb-space-integral-qcqs-permanence]. Separatedness follows by restricting the closed diagonal of $a$ after base change. Its geometric fibre cardinalities are bounded by $d$. By [lem-sfb-space-etale-closed-degree-loci], the locus where their cardinalities are at most $d-1$ is closed. Step 5 shows it contains the dense open $U$, hence it is all of $B$. Apply the induction hypothesis to $W\to V$ with bound $d-1$: the target $V$ is qcqs and the scheme $W$ is quasi-compact and separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. We obtain a scheme $Z$ with a surjective integral map $Z\to V$ which Zariski locally factors through $W$.

The open inclusion $V\hookrightarrow B$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-integral-qcqs-permanence], since $V$ is quasi-compact and $B$ quasi-separated. Apply [lem-sfb-space-integral-extension-qc-open] to $Z\to V$ and obtain an integral $E\to B$ with $E\times_BV=Z$. The open immersion $Z\hookrightarrow E$ is quasi-compact: $Z$ is quasi-compact since it is integral over the quasi-compact space $V$, while $E$ is quasi-separated since it is integral over the qcqs space $B$; apply [lem-sfb-space-integral-qcqs-permanence] to $Z\to E$. Replace $E$ by the schematic closure of $Z$, using [lem-sfb-space-qc-open-schematic-closure]. Since $Z$ is already closed in $E\times_BV=Z$, restriction of that closure to $V$ remains exactly $Z$. The map $E\to B$ remains integral: a closed immersion is integral and integral scheme morphisms compose on each scheme test by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc].

The two open subspaces $Z=E\times_BV$ and $E\times_BU$ cover $E$, because $U\cup V=B$. The first is a scheme by induction; the second is a scheme since it is integral over the scheme $U$, by [lem-sfb-space-integral-qcqs-permanence]. Hence [lem-pc-schemes-criterion] implies that $E$ is a scheme: the algebraic-space sheaf is a Zariski sheaf, these are representable open subfunctors, and their pullbacks cover every scheme test. Its map to $X$ locally factors through $U$: over $E\times_BU$ use its projection to $U$; over $Z$ use the local factorizations $Z\to W\subseteq U\times_XB\to U$ from induction. The composites with $a$ are the map $E\to B\to X$ by the fibre-product identities.

Take the reduced closed subspace $T\hookrightarrow B$ supported on $B\setminus V$, supplied by [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support]. Its map factors through $U$ because this closed subset is contained in $U$. The base change to $U$ is therefore $T$ itself, a closed subscheme of $U$; thus $T$ is a scheme. Let $H=E\amalg T$ be the scheme coproduct [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Both maps to $B$ are integral, using the closed-immersion clause of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc] for $T$. Their coproduct is integral: over an affine scheme test of $B$ its source is the spectrum of the product of the two integral algebras; affineness of this finite disjoint union is the final clause of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. For $(b,c)$ annihilated by monic polynomials $F$ and $G$, the monic product $FG$ annihilates $(b,c)$, proving integrality. Composing with the integral $B\to X$ is integral by the same cited scheme composition theorem on each test.

The image of $E\to B$ contains $V$ because its restriction is the surjection $Z\to V$, and $T$ covers $B\setminus V$. Hence $H\to B$ is surjective. The image of $B\to X$ contains the image of $U\to X$, which is all of $X$, so $H\to X$ is surjective. The local factorizations through $U$ on $E$ were constructed in step 8, and on $T$ there is a global factorization through $U$. They persist on the two open summands of $H$. This completes the strong induction assertion. Applied to the affine atlas of step 1, it gives the required surjective integral map from the $S$-scheme $H$ to $X$. All constructions and maps were over $S$.
